attributes.description: The son of Daśaratha who rules Ayodhyá as a regent from Nandigrám, wearing hermit's dress and matted hair.
The eldest son of Daśaratha, constant in his vow to remain in exile for fourteen years.
The daughter of King Janak, found in a furrow of the earth; a devotee of saintly life.
The aged, saintly wife of Atri who performed ten thousand years of penance and gifted Sítá celestial cosmetics and robes.
A high-souled hermit whose hermitage Ráma visits after leaving Chitrakúta.
A giant demon and brother of RávaG who dwells in Janasthán and harasses the hermits.
The capital city, described as dark and desolate in the absence of Ráma.
The town where Bharat establishes his seat of government to avoid ruling from the capital.
Gold-wrought emblems of Ráma's authority, placed on the throne by Bharat.
A part of the Daṇḍak forest plagued by man-eating demons.

attributes.context: Bharat refers all state affairs to the sandals as emblems of Ráma.
Ráma remains in exile to fulfill his father's decree.
Husband and wife dwelling in a pure retreat.
Anasúyá grants Sítá a celestial robe and an eternal beauty balsam.
Bharat lives here in exile as a hermit until Ráma returns.
Khara venges with fury all those who dwell in Janasthán.
Janak found Sítá in a furrow and raised her as his daughter.
Ráma won Sítá's hand by snapping the great bow of mountain size.
